rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Rules version: 6
rules.says: The rules file carries a version number (here 6) that plans point to and that is raised whenever the rules change.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: This file is the one copy of the rules every plan used to copy into itself. An agent's prompt is only the plan's path and a step number, so an agent reads this file by its full path
rules.says: An agent's prompt is only the plan's path and a step number, so before anything else it reads the rules file by its full path, /root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md.
rules.live_quote: Read the short page first, at /home/user/noahjefferson/plans/native/page.md, as your first call and alone, and follow it.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: and the plan carries only its own work.
rules.says: A plan carries only its own work and does not copy the shared rules into itself, because this file is the one copy of them.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: An agent's prompt is only the plan's path and a step number
rules.says: An agent's prompt is only the plan's path and a step number, so everything else an agent needs comes from the plan and this rules file, which it reads first.
rules.live_quote: A worker is told the page and its step, nothing more.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A plan with a `## Steps` section has a `## Rules` section holding either the pointer line below or every rule line of this file
rules.says: Any plan with a Steps section must have a Rules section holding either the pointer line or every rule line of this file, and a plan whose section is neither is refused.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The pointer names the version of this file the owner read. While the file's version is not the plan's, the dispatch gate (`rulesGate`) sends no step
rules.says: The pointer names the rules version the owner read, and while the file's version differs from the plan's no step is sent, so agents follow the rules the plan was approved with.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A change to the rules below raises the version, and lands only when no plan is in force, as the last step of the plan that makes it
rules.says: A change to the rules raises the version and may land only when no plan is in force, as the last step of the plan that makes the change.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: no plan is moved to a new rules version without the button, because the Rules line is part of the approved scope.
rules.says: No plan is moved to a new rules version without the owner's button press, because the Rules line is part of the approved scope.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The pointer line, as a plan writes it:
rules.says: A plan writes its pointer line in the exact form 'Rules: /root/.claude/hub/agent-rules.md, version N.' (shown with version 1).

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The rules, one per line. A plan may add rules of its own beside the pointer, and may never take one away.
rules.says: A plan may add rules of its own beside the pointer but may never remove or weaken any rule of this file.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Never `cd`, and never pushd or popd either, at any depth.
rules.says: An agent never uses cd, pushd or popd at any depth.
rules.live_quote: Write every path in full and never change directory, not even inside a longer command: git takes -C and npm takes --prefix.
rules.missing: pushd and popd are not named anywhere live; only never changing directory is stated.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Write every path in full.
rules.says: Every path an agent writes is written in full (absolute).
rules.live_quote: Write every path in full and never change directory, not even inside a longer command: git takes -C and npm takes --prefix.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Every file is read with the Read or Grep tool, never through Bash.
rules.says: An agent reads every file with the Read or Grep tool and never through Bash.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Bash runs only a command the step's Commands line names, the git reads among them
rules.says: Bash runs only a command that the step's Commands line names (the permitted git reads count among them) and nothing else.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: one command per call and never joined to another with `&&`, `;` or a pipe.
rules.says: Each Bash call holds exactly one command, never joined to another with &&, ; or a pipe.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: No command carries a variable assignment in front of it
rules.says: No command an agent runs carries a variable assignment in front of it.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: and no agent reads a clock: the status command stamps every time the owner sees.
rules.says: No agent reads a clock, because the status command stamps every time the owner sees.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: `git push` carries no redirect and no pipe after it.
rules.says: A git push command carries no redirect and no pipe after it.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: NO HEX WRITTEN. No write by an agent, to any file, carries a run of seven or more characters from the set 0 to 9 and a to f that no command exiting zero printed in that agent's own run.
rules.says: No write by an agent to any file may carry a run of seven or more characters from 0-9 and a-f unless a command that exited zero printed that run in the agent's own run.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A plant, a label, a fixture or a stand-in value is plain words with a letter outside that set in every seven characters.
rules.says: A plant, label, fixture or stand-in value is written as plain words with a letter outside the 0-9 a-f set in every seven characters.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Every constant is written as a decimal number, never as a hex literal.
rules.says: Every constant is written as a decimal number and never as a hex literal.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A STEP IS FOUR PARTS, AND THE AGENT READS THEM FIRST, IN THIS ORDER.
rules.says: A step has four parts (Facts, Do, Observe, Kill) and the agent reads them first, in that order.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Facts: the asks and the app facts the step depends on, restated; the step is judged against them and an agent that finds one false ejects.
rules.says: Facts restates the asks and app facts the step depends on; the step is judged against them, and an agent that finds one false ejects.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Do: the exact actions, and nothing outside them.
rules.says: Do holds the exact actions, and the agent does nothing outside them.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Observe: the observation that means the step is done; the step is DONE when that is seen and not before.
rules.says: Observe names the observation that means the step is done, and the step is DONE only when that observation is seen, not before.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Kill: what ends the step with nothing further written.
rules.says: Kill names what ends the step with nothing further written.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A step on the plan's Standing line carries none of the four and is read as it is written (the review follows `/root/.claude/hub/aim-review.md`).
rules.says: A step on the plan's Standing line carries none of the four parts and is read as written, and the review step follows /root/.claude/hub/aim-review.md.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: THE REPORT IS WRITTEN AS THE WORK LANDS. `progress/step-N-report.txt` in the session scratchpad is written with the Write tool after each stage, whole each time, before the next command runs
rules.says: The report progress/step-N-report.txt in the session scratchpad is written with the Write tool after each stage, whole each time, before the next command runs.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: a re-sent agent reads it first and resumes from it.
rules.says: An agent that is re-sent on a step reads its existing report first and resumes from it.
rules.live_quote: When you are sent on again, read your earlier output before repeating a command.
rules.missing: The report file progress/step-N-report.txt is not named; resuming from the report is not stated, only reading earlier output before repeating a command.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The progress note `progress/step-N.txt` is written the same way.
rules.says: The progress note progress/step-N.txt is written the same way as the report (Write tool, whole, after each stage, before the next command).

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The hand-back is two lines: one word, DONE, REFUSED, FAILED or EJECT, then the wall line
rules.says: The hand-back is two lines, a single verdict word (DONE, REFUSED, FAILED or EJECT) and then the wall line, except the Standing review step, which opens with its verdict line and carries its own wall line second.
rules.live_quote: The first word of the report is DONE, FAILED or REFUSED.
rules.missing: EJECT as a verdict word, the two-line hand-back form, the wall line after the verdict word, and the Standing review exception.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The report's first line is the same word and its second line is the same wall line.
rules.says: The report's first line is the same verdict word as the hand-back and its second line is the same wall line.
rules.live_quote: The first word of the report is DONE, FAILED or REFUSED.
rules.missing: The second line being the same wall line, and the report's verdict matching the hand-back.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The report ends with a line beginning `Found:` for each thing found and not fixed.
rules.says: The report ends with one line beginning 'Found:' for each thing found and not fixed.
rules.live_quote: Report, in this order: what was done, what was seen, the files changed, and anything found and not fixed, each on a line opening with Found.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: The Standing review step writes its own record to `progress/step-N-review-K.txt`, where K is one more than the number of such files for that step already there (found with Glob)
rules.says: The Standing review step writes its record to progress/step-N-review-K.txt, with K one more than the count of such files already present (counted with Glob), so a later review never overwrites an earlier one.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: THE WALL LINE IS ONE SENTENCE, FIRST AFTER THE VERDICT WORD IN EVERY REPORT AND HAND-BACK.
rules.says: Every report and hand-back carries a wall line of one sentence, placed first after the verdict word.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: It answers three questions: whether the step still serves the plan's goal 1, whether that goal still serves the owner's asks as the plan's Design states them, and whether what the step saw moved either answer.
rules.says: The wall line answers whether the step still serves the plan's goal 1, whether that goal still serves the owner's asks as the Design states them, and whether what the step saw moved either answer; a no to either of the first two, or a yes to the third, is an eject.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A RED CHECK IS REPAIRED ONCE BY THE AGENT THAT MADE IT, OR IT ENDS THE STEP. A command that exits non-zero, or an observation that is not the one the step's Observe names, is a red check.
rules.says: A command exiting non-zero or an observation other than the one Observe names is a red check, which the agent that made it may repair once or else it ends the step.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Where its cause is read from the run's own output and lies in a file this agent has itself written in this send, the agent repairs it once
rules.says: Only where the cause is read from the run's own output and lies in a file the agent itself wrote in this send, the agent writes into its report what was red and its cause, edits only that file, and runs the red check again once.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A second red check in the send, a cause that cannot be read from the output, or a cause in any other file ends the step
rules.says: A second red check in the send, a cause not readable from the output, or a cause in any other file ends the step: the agent writes what it saw into its report (the only writes allowed afterward are the report and progress note), hands back FAILED naming it, and does nothing more.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: No repair removes or loosens an assertion: a case is changed only to the behaviour the step's own text asks for.
rules.says: A repair never removes or loosens an assertion; a test case is changed only to the behaviour the step's own text asks for.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A command that exited non-zero is run again only after such a repair, and never a third time.
rules.says: A command that exited non-zero is re-run only after such a repair and never a third time.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A scratch script prints what it found and exits 0 whatever it finds.
rules.says: A scratch script prints what it found and exits 0 whatever it finds.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Where a failed command's captured output carries the container's proxy notice for a host, the reading is recorded before any other call of the agent, with `node /root/.claude/hub/reply-guard.mjs --read <host>
rules.says: When a failed command's captured output carries the container's proxy notice for a host, the agent records the reading before any other call using node /root/.claude/hub/reply-guard.mjs --read <host> --said "<notice copied character for character>" --route "owner: <what stays blocked>", and where the captured notice differs from the usual one the captured notice wins.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: EJECT IS THE HAND-BACK FOR WHAT THE STEP DID NOT FORESEE. An observation the step's text did not name, or a judgement the step's text does not settle, ends the step as an eject to the plan
rules.says: An observation the step's text did not name, or a judgement it does not settle, ends the step as an eject: the agent writes what was seen and the files it names into its report, hands back EJECT with the wall line, and writes nothing after.
rules.live_quote: If the step seems to need something outside it, stop and say so.
rules.missing: Eject as a hand-back distinct from DONE and FAILED, writing what was seen and the files named into the report, the wall line, and the rule for an observation or judgement the step did not name.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: EJECT is neither DONE nor FAILED: the plan is rewritten from the files the report names, the pointer stays on the step, and the step is sent again.
rules.says: EJECT is distinct from DONE and FAILED: the plan is rewritten from the files the report names, the pointer stays on the step, and the step is sent again.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: An unforeseen thing is never settled by the agent's own choice.
rules.says: An agent never settles an unforeseen thing by its own choice.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: At any refusal, stop and hand back REFUSED, with the refusal's text in the report file if it can still be written and in the hand-back otherwise.
rules.says: At any refusal the agent stops and hands back REFUSED, with the refusal's text in the report file if it can still be written and in the hand-back otherwise.
rules.live_quote: A refusal from a hook or the harness is an instruction. Stop that route, say plainly what was refused, and do not try another way to the same end.
rules.missing: Handing back REFUSED at a refusal, and the refusal's text going in the report file if it can be written and in the hand-back otherwise; live only says to say plainly what was refused.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A different command for the same end is a second route, and refused.
rules.says: A different command used for the same end after a refusal is a second route and is refused, so an agent never works around a refusal.
rules.live_quote: Stop that route, say plainly what was refused, and do not try another way to the same end.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Do the named step and nothing outside it.
rules.says: An agent does the named step and nothing outside it.
rules.live_quote: Do that step and nothing outside it. If the step seems to need something outside it, stop and say so.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Every scratch script prints, before its own results, a MADE TO FAIL block whose lines are `console.log` calls written out in the script
rules.says: Every scratch script prints, before its own results, a MADE TO FAIL block of console.log calls written out in the script with their words inside each call.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: the first carrying the words MADE TO FAIL, a known figure written in digits that the instrument must reproduce, and one line carrying the words "nothing below is trustworthy"
rules.says: The MADE TO FAIL block's first line carries the words MADE TO FAIL, it includes a known figure in digits that the instrument must reproduce, and one line carries the words "nothing below is trustworthy".

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: never through a helper function, a variable or a template.
rules.says: The MADE TO FAIL lines are never produced through a helper function, a variable or a template.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: EVERY FILE UNDER THE SCRATCHPAD IS RUN THROUGH A HARNESS. The harness guard takes any node run on a file under the session scratchpad, a worktree's tracked files included, for a scratch harness, and refuses it without the MADE TO FAIL block.
rules.says: The harness guard treats any node run on a file under the session scratchpad (including a worktree's tracked files) as a scratch harness and refuses it without the MADE TO FAIL block.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: So a check or test of a worktree file is a child process of a scratch harness that carries the block, never a node command naming that file.
rules.says: A check or test of a worktree file is run as a child process of a scratch harness that carries the MADE TO FAIL block, never as a node command naming that file.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A RUN THAT MAY OUTLAST TEN MINUTES RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND, writing its output to a file in the scratchpad that is read when it ends.
rules.says: A run that may outlast ten minutes runs in the background, writing its output to a file in the scratchpad that is read when the run ends.
rules.live_quote: If a run must be in the background, do not hand back until it has ended and you have read its output.
rules.missing: The ten-minute threshold that sends a run to the background, and writing its output to a scratchpad file; live says run in the foreground by default.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: Never quote the owner in any file, and never copy the transcript or any owner message into a file; read the transcript in place.
rules.says: An agent never quotes the owner in any file and never copies the transcript or any owner message into a file; the transcript is read in place.
rules.live_quote: The owner is never quoted while doing it, and no owner message is copied into any file.
rules.missing: Never copying the transcript into a file, and reading the transcript in place; the live line is in never.md, not in the short page the agents read.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A verdict or a report says what the owner wants in the agent's own words.
rules.says: A verdict or report states what the owner wants in the agent's own words.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: No line an agent writes into a repository attributes a message, a report or a decision to the owner, by name, by role or by a possessive
rules.says: No line an agent writes into a repository attributes a message, report or decision to the owner by name, role or possessive; what the session received is written as a message the session was given.
rules.live_quote: Nothing in any file quotes or names the repository's owner, or attributes a message to the owner.
rules.missing: Attribution of a report or decision (not only a message), attribution by role or by a possessive, and writing what the session received as a message the session was given.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: For git state, use the reads the fence counts: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, `git log`, `git status`, `git diff`, `git show`, `git rev-parse`, a bare `git branch`, `git remote -v`.
rules.says: For git state an agent uses only the reads the fence counts: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, git log, git status, git diff, git show, git rev-parse, a bare git branch, and git remote -v.

rules.heading: Rules for every agent
rules.quote: A step that lists its commands runs those, in that order, and nothing else.
rules.says: A step that lists its commands runs exactly those commands, in that order, and nothing else.
